summary: Build responsible AI credit models for thin-file borrowers using alternative data, validation, and governance. Enrol in the practical course.
lede: AI-driven inclusive credit scoring and digital lending equips lenders to assess borrowers beyond traditional credit files while managing risks such as non-performing loans, unfair treatment, and supervisory scrutiny. You will work through alternative-data profiling, feature engineering, scorecard development, validation, fairness testing, and portfolio monitoring using structured credit processes and practical analytics tools. The course applies the NIST AI Risk Management Framework alongside Basel Committee credit risk principles and IFRS 9 expectations for traceable assumptions, documentation, monitoring, and provisioning logic. You will practise calculating Gini and AUC, creating a model card, testing cut-off strategies, and mapping deployment controls into a credit workflow, leaving with working templates, a model risk register, a monitoring dashboard specification, and an implementation roadmap.
audienceIntro: AI credit underwriting training is designed for professionals who make, validate, govern, supervise, or operationalize lending decisions involving incomplete borrower information. It suits experienced practitioners and technically capable professionals who need a shared language across credit, analytics, technology, and oversight functions.
audience: Central Bank and Financial Supervisory Officers
prerequisites: You should have working knowledge of credit assessment, loan origination, portfolio monitoring, or financial risk management. Familiarity with spreadsheets and basic data interpretation helps, but advanced programming is not required. Coding is not required for completion because demonstrations and guided notebook exercises use prepared examples. Advanced machine learning topics receive conceptual awareness and operational application rather than production engineering depth.
topics: Digital financial services, payments & fintech risk
